description: Third-round research-only temporal candidates for Canada military/facility overlay records that remain undated after the current webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_base_temporal_overrides.json file. This pass focuses on residual Arctic/radar/station/camp/training-area records and intentionally skips uncertain name matches.
scope_notes: Input records were checked against data/reports/military_base_temporal_priority_queue.json, webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_bases.geojson, and webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_base_temporal_overrides.json.
Only country_code CA overlay records with no current temporal override were included.
Camp-Bouchard was skipped because geonames:5914215 already has a current override.

Pelly Island/Nipterk Base was skipped because the strongest sources found in this pass tied Nipterk/Pelly to oil/exploration, weather, or generic GeoNames-style listings rather than a reliable military operational history.

candidates.name: Canadian Forces Station Flin Flon

operational_intervals.label: Canadian Forces Supplementary Radio System / CFS Flin Flon phase

source_notes.title: Semaphore to Satellite, Chapter 11 - A Story of Canadian Military Communications
source_notes.note: The communications-history chapter states that Stage Two of Canadian Forces integration created the Canadian Forces Supplementary Radio System in 1966, lists Flin Flon among the former RCAF stations that became CFS sites, and says CFS Flin Flon ceased operations in March 1973.

source_notes.title: Gravity (CGSN) - Natural Resources Canada
source_notes.note: NRCan's geodetic station page identifies the location as FLIN FLON (CFS) and describes access at the CFS base near Creighton, supporting the exact station-site match.

candidates.rationale: Exact English overlay record at the CFS Flin Flon coordinates. The start/end years are limited to the documented CFS phase rather than inferring an earlier RCAF start.

candidates.name: Station des Forces canadiennes Flin Flon

operational_intervals.label: Canadian Forces Supplementary Radio System / Station des Forces canadiennes Flin Flon phase

source_notes.title: Semaphore to Satellite, Chapter 11 - A Story of Canadian Military Communications
source_notes.note: The source supports the 1966 CFSRS conversion and March 1973 cessation of operations for CFS Flin Flon.

source_notes.title: Gravity (CGSN) - Natural Resources Canada
source_notes.note: NRCan confirms the CFS Flin Flon station location near the overlay coordinates.

candidates.rationale: French overlay alias at the same coordinates as Canadian Forces Station Flin Flon; the same CFS-phase chronology applies.

candidates.name: Lac-Saint-Denis

operational_intervals.label: RCAF Station Lac St. Denis / Pinetree Line radar-station phase

source_notes.title: RCAF Station Lac St. Denis - FortWiki Historic U.S. and Canadian Forts
source_notes.note: FortWiki identifies Lac St. Denis as a 1952-1986 Pinetree Line radar station, says it became operational on July 1, 1952, was renamed CFS Lac St. Denis after unification, and closed in 1986.

source_notes.title: The Pinetree Line: CFS Lac St. Denis - Morin Heights Historical Association
source_notes.note: The local historical association says the base was built from 1949 to 1952, officially opened on July 1, 1952, and finally closed in 1986.

candidates.rationale: The overlay label is shortened to the place name, but its coordinates align with the former CFS Lac St. Denis radar station. The candidate uses the documented operational radar-station span.

candidates.name: Canadian Forces Base Montréal

source_notes.title: Building 42 - Parks Canada Federal Heritage Buildings Review Office
source_notes.note: Parks Canada places Building 42 at Garrison Longue Pointe (CFB Montreal), gives its construction date as 1941, and associates it with the establishment of Garrison Longue-Pointe during the Second World War as a supply depot.

source_notes.title: Building 42 - Canada's Historic Places
source_notes.note: Canada's Historic Places likewise identifies the CFB Montreal/Garrison Longue-Pointe administration building with a 1941 construction date and Second World War supply-depot association.

candidates.rationale: Exact overlay coordinates match the Longue-Pointe/CFB Montreal site. The candidate uses the documented 1941 military supply-depot establishment for site visibility rather than trying to infer a later administrative renaming year.

candidates.name: Base des Forces canadiennes Montréal

source_notes.title: Building 42 - Parks Canada Federal Heritage Buildings Review Office
source_notes.note: Parks Canada supports the 1941 Longue-Pointe/CFB Montreal military supply-depot origin.

source_notes.title: Building 42 - Canada's Historic Places
source_notes.note: The national register page confirms the same Garrison Longue-Pointe (CFB Montreal) site association.

candidates.rationale: French overlay alias at the same coordinates as Canadian Forces Base Montréal; the Longue-Pointe site-origin chronology applies.

candidates.name: Base militaire de Saint-Jean

source_notes.title: Ville militaire, ville garnison - Ville de Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu
source_notes.note: The municipal history says the Canadian Armed Forces arrived in 1941, that the Saint-Jean military base was built at the start of the Second World War for navigator/bomber training, and that National Defence reacquired the site in 1951 for permanent Canadian Forces use.

source_notes.title: RCAF Station St Jean - RCAF.Info
source_notes.note: RCAF.Info lists RCAF Station St Jean as in use from 1941 to present and says No. 9 Air Observer School opened at St Jean on July 7, 1941.

source_notes.title: École de leadership et de recrues des Forces canadiennes - Canada.ca
source_notes.note: Canada.ca confirms the current Canadian Forces Leadership and Recruit School presence at Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu.

candidates.rationale: Exact French overlay label and coordinates for the Saint-Jean military-base site. The candidate uses the documented 1941 wartime military arrival and leaves the endpoint open because official current pages confirm continuing CAF training use.

candidates.name: Wainwright Regional Training Area

source_notes.title: 3rd Canadian Division Support Base Detachment Wainwright - Canada.ca
source_notes.note: Canada.ca identifies Detachment Wainwright as one of Canada's busiest Army bases and says CFB/ASU Wainwright pastures its bison herd in a protected part of the range and training area.

source_notes.title: Bud Cotton Buffalo Paddock - Canadian Forces Morale and Welfare Services
source_notes.note: CFMWS history says Camp Wainwright was established at the former Buffalo National Park location in 1940.

candidates.rationale: Exact English overlay record for the Wainwright range/training area. The source-backed 1940 Camp Wainwright establishment year and current Canada.ca training-area status support an open-ended candidate.

source_notes.title: 3rd Canadian Division Support Base Detachment Wainwright - Canada.ca
source_notes.note: Canada.ca confirms current Detachment Wainwright and its range/training-area function.

source_notes.title: Bud Cotton Buffalo Paddock - Canadian Forces Morale and Welfare Services
source_notes.note: CFMWS provides the 1940 Camp Wainwright establishment year.

candidates.name: Mary Hill Training Area

operational_intervals.label: Mary Hill training area / DND-managed CFB Esquimalt property phase

source_notes.title: Public Service Announcements - District of Metchosin / Department of National Defence and Royal Canadian Navy notices
source_notes.note: DND/RCN notices identify Mary Hill Training Area in Metchosin, say the Royal Canadian Navy has used the property for military training since the 1930s, and describe current CAF dry-training use.

source_notes.title: Mary Hill Battery - FortWiki Historic U.S. and Canadian Forts
source_notes.note: FortWiki documents the Mary Hill Battery as armed in 1939, decommissioned in 1956, and still existing on the Mary Hill training area as part of CFB Esquimalt.

source_notes.title: Recovery Strategy for the Rigid Apple Moss in Canada - Canada.ca
source_notes.note: Canada.ca identifies Mary Hill Training Area as a property managed by the Department of National Defence / CFB Esquimalt.

candidates.rationale: Exact overlay name and coordinates match the DND-managed Mary Hill training area. The 1939 start is anchored to the battery documented at the same site, while current training-area use is separately supported by DND/RCN notices.

candidates.name: Albert Head Battery Point Training Area

operational_intervals.label: Albert Head coastal artillery battery phase
Albert Head Canadian Forces range/training-area phase

source_notes.title: Place names - Albert Head Battery Point Training Area - Natural Resources Canada
source_notes.note: NRCan identifies Albert Head Battery Point Training Area as an official Canadian Forces Range and/or Training Area sourced to National Defence.

source_notes.title: British Columbia - Canadian Military History
source_notes.note: The site history says Albert Head was originally established as an artillery coastal battery from 1938 to 1946 and now serves as a summer training camp, Canadian Ranger site, and CFB Esquimalt range-control area.

source_notes.title: Public Service Announcements - District of Metchosin / Department of National Defence and Royal Canadian Navy notices
source_notes.note: DND/RCN notices describe current training activity at the Albert Head Training Area.

candidates.rationale: Exact English overlay record for the official NRCan/DND training-area feature. The 1938 start comes from a site-history source, so confidence is medium rather than high.
